summary: Self-serve: register an OAuth app in your account settings and get a client ID and secret immediately. No approval step was found in the sources read.
prod_ready: Same day (no review gate found; see claims)
composio_note: Composio's GitHub toolkit page lists managed OAuth (OAuth2) as available, checked 2026-10-31. If you use Composio, you can connect GitHub without registering your own OAuth app. Register your own only for your brand on the consent screen, custom scopes, or a separate rate-limit quota.
before_you_start: A GitHub account (personal or an organization where you are admin).
Add a redirect URI for each environment (local, staging, production). The settings page allows up to 10.
setup_steps: Settings > Developer settings > OAuth Apps > New OAuth App.
Fill application name, homepage URL and optional description (use only public information).
Set the Authorization callback URL to your app's exact redirect URI. You can add up to 10.
Optionally enable Device Flow. Decide whether to keep 'Expire user access tokens' on (the default), which needs refresh-token support in your code. Then click Register application.
Copy the client ID and generate a client secret.

review.what: No marketplace-style review found for OAuth apps in the docs read. Organizations may restrict third-party app access (inferred, not sourced).
rejection_risks: Org owners can block unapproved OAuth apps, so users in locked-down orgs may need an admin to approve.

agent: Draft the exact field values and redirect URI per environment.
Generate the code for the authorize/token exchange.
you: Click through the registration (needs your logged-in account).

blockers.fix: Every redirect URI must match exactly. Add each environment's URI to the same app, and avoid wildcard matching unless you control every possible match.

blockers.problem: User access tokens stop working after a short time
blockers.fix: 'Expire user access tokens' is on by default. Store the refresh token and refresh access tokens, or uncheck the option only if your code cannot handle short-lived tokens yet.

blockers.problem: Users in an org cannot authorize
blockers.fix: Ask an org owner to approve your app under the org's third-party access settings (inferred).

summary: Easy to start in Testing mode, hard to ship. Sensitive scopes need app verification, and restricted scopes (most Gmail and Drive) also need an annual third-party security assessment.
dev_ready: ~1 hour (Testing mode, up to 100 test users)
prod_ready: Sensitive scopes: roughly a week. Restricted scopes: roughly 2 to 4+ weeks including the security assessment
composio_note: Composio's Gmail and Google Drive toolkit pages list managed OAuth (OAuth2) as available, checked 2026-10-31. If you use Composio you may not need your own Google OAuth app for a first connection. Register your own for your brand on the consent screen, custom scopes, or your own quota. What the managed app's consent screen shows users was not checked.
before_you_start: A Google Cloud project and a verified app domain with a privacy policy.
Pick the narrowest scopes possible; reviewers reject unused scopes.
Budget for a CASA assessment vendor if you need restricted scopes (fee not verified).
setup_steps: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the APIs you need.
Configure the OAuth consent screen and add the scopes under Data Access.
Create an OAuth client ID and copy the secret (shown once).
Test in Testing mode with listed test users.
Publish to production, click Prepare for Verification, justify scopes and upload a demo video.
If restricted scopes: complete the CASA assessment with an approved vendor, then renew annually.

review.what: Brand verification for sensitive scopes; verification plus CASA security assessment for restricted scopes.
rejection_risks: Requesting scopes the app does not use.
Demo video that does not show the full OAuth flow and scope usage.
Unpatched findings from the security scan.

agent: Pick minimum scopes, draft scope justifications and the demo-video script, prepare the privacy policy checklist.
you: Create the project, verify the domain, record the demo video, pay and coordinate the CASA vendor.
provider: Google reviews the app; the CASA vendor performs the assessment.

blockers.fix: In Testing mode, add them as a test user (max 100), or publish and verify.

blockers.problem: Integration works, then breaks after a week
blockers.fix: Testing-mode refresh tokens expire after 7 days. Move to production before real users.
The count cannot be reset; use a separate Cloud project for development.
